439
# Saves: vim's rename-write-delete and Word's temp swap keep the file's node across scans, with and without sending between scans, while the first upload or a second save is in flight, with two saves in a row or overlapping and cleaned up in separate scans, when the temp file synced before its last write, when the backup is deleted one scan later or at the end of the removal wait. Main loses the node in each of these, and no earlier test runs a save across scans.
# Saves: the rule's limits keep each file's own history. A backup that stays or is written again, an older or recently revised file moved onto the name from another name, a case-only rename, a file moved to an excluded name on purpose, overlapping backups removed in one batch, and a daemon restart between a save's steps each read as main does, with no content lost and no extra node on the server. These come from the primary and adversarial reviews, which found each one breaking an earlier head.
# Second device: a vim save followed step by step on another device ends with that device holding the new bytes and one node. No earlier test follows a save from a second device.
